subject: BlueCrest Labs — critical path: latency spike & throughput errors
messages:
From: BlueCrest - OnCall <infra@bluecrestlabs.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia@bluecrestlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION] Production latency spike and 5xx surge (region us-west)

Maya / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden, sustained latency spike across our inference calls (p95 rising from ~180ms to ~1.6s) starting ~07:50 PDT and a corresponding rise in 5xx errors (from 0.2% to ~4.7%). This is impacting our checkout flow. We've collected a heapdump and the attached short log excerpt.

Immediate impact: 10% of user sessions are timing out and retries amplify load.
What we've tried: client-side backoff; throttling to a single shard — no effect.

We need an ETA and current remediation plan from Redwood. Please escalate to on-call + exec if required.

Attachments: heapdump-20270621.txt (log excerpt)

--
Lydia Park
SRE Lead, BlueCrest Labs
lidia@bluecrestlabs.com
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia@bluecrestlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:20:15 -0700
Subject: RE: [ACTION] Production latency spike and 5xx surge (region us-west)

Folks — bringing this into an internal exec-liaison cadence. BlueCrest reports elevated latency & 5xx in us-west. Initial attachments show memory churn + dropped connections.

Plan (first 30 mins):
- Marissa: triage kernel-level errors + confirm whether this is model runtime or networking (priority).
- Karthik: evaluate routing fallback to dedicated pool and whether a traffic split reduces tail latency.
- Grace: pull telemetry (per-route p95/p99, node utilization) and prepare a one-page for execs.
- Aditya: prepare customer-facing status and list of mitigation options (short + medium).

Meet: 08:35 PDT in Zoom (link in calendar) — join if you can. I will own customer comms after we have a short mitigation.

If anyone thinks we should immediately failover to the compatible smaller model variant, call it out in thread.

--
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:28:42 -0700
Subject: RE: [ACTION] Production latency spike and 5xx surge (region us-west)

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 08:20, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Folks — bringing this into an internal exec-liaison cadence.

Quick technical update from triage:
- Observed symptom: KV cache eviction is spiking under certain prefix distributions; this is causing frequent cold-cache model unlocks and higher per-token latency.
- 5xx root signals: transient OOM spikes on two nodes (rt-uw-11 & rt-uw-14) coincident with long GC pauses. Heapdump attached (heapdump-20270621.txt).
- Immediate action taken: rolled back the recent kernel patch on the affected pool at 08:12 PDT (partial rollback on 6 nodes). Early telemetry shows a small reduction in OOMs but p95 still elevated.

Next steps (engineering):
1) Continue rollback across remaining nodes (estimated 20 min).
2) Throttle concurrent streams per connection to reduce KV churn (hotfix).
3) If rollback + throttle not sufficient in 20–30m, plan B is routing heavy routes to dedicated pool (Karthik to action).

I'll send a short patch/rollback note to the thread when I finish.

Attachments: patch-rollback-notes-21jun.pdf

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:47:09 -0700
Subject: RE: [ACTION] Production latency spike and 5xx surge (region us-west)

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 08:28, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Quick technical update from triage:

Thanks — routing option ready. If rollback + throttle doesn't bring p95 below 400ms in the next 20m, we can: 
- Shift 30% of BlueCrest traffic to the dedicated us-west pool (reserved capacity) and apply a gentle rate-limit to minimize burst amplification.
- Apply automatic KV-prefetch for BlueCrest prefix families (best-effort) to reduce cold-cache behavior.

Operational considerations:
- Dedicated routing requires a quick capacity check & approval to allow burst beyond committed limits. That will need APAC Sales or Finance sign-off for short window credits if we exceed reserved caps.
- Grace: can you flatten a per-route token-cost projection (30% shift) so we can include estimated chargebacks?

I can prepare a 1-slide exec ask for a minute.

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated & Capacity
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwoodinference.com>
To: BlueCrest - OnCall <infra@bluecrestlabs.com>, Lydia Park <lydia@bluecrestlabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 01:03:00 -07:00
Subject: BlueCrest — Immediate update and short-term mitigation steps

Lydia / BlueCrest team,

Thanks for the alert and the heapdump — we agree this is a priority and wanted to share where we are and our near-term plan: 

Summary of what happened:
- Root cause (preliminary): elevated KV cache eviction causing cold-cache unlocks combined with GC-induced OOMs on a subset of runtime nodes after a recent kernel tuning change.
- Impact: elevated p95 / p99 latency and a transient 5xx spike.

What we've done so far (last 6 hours):
- Partial rollback of the recent kernel patch on affected nodes; live rollback continuing across the pool.
- Applied throttling to concurrent streams to reduce KV churn.
- Prepared patch notes and heapdump analysis (attached).

Immediate mitigation plan (next 60–90 minutes):
1) Complete rollback across remaining nodes (target: 09:10 PDT).
2) If p95 remains > 400ms after rollback, we will route ~30% of your traffic to our dedicated us-west pool to reduce tail exposure (this is non-destructive and reversible).
3) We'll keep a dedicated liaison (Maya) and provide 15-min cadence updates until stable.

Customer asks / asks of BlueCrest:
- Please confirm whether you can tolerate a brief routing split (non-disruptive) if we need to take step 2.
- If you have additional telemetry (client-side retry logs), please share — that helps validate mitigation impact.

We will follow up in 15 minutes with telemetry and expected ETA. Apologies for the impact; we're treating this as top-priority.

Attachments: exec-brief-BlueCrest-21jun.docx, patch-rollback-notes-21jun.pdf

Regards,

--
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
